entries.name: ct.models.MLModel
entries.notes: Load a CoreML model from .mlmodel or .mlpackage. Uses ANE/GPU/CPU automatically.

entries.name: MLModel.predict
entries.notes: Run inference. Dispatches to ANE (Neural Engine), GPU (Metal), or CPU based on model ops. For vision models: input is typically {'image': PIL.Image}.

entries.name: ct.converters.convert
entries.notes: Convert PyTorch/TF/ONNX to CoreML. mlprogram format required for ANE. compute_units='ALL' enables ANE.

entries.name: ct.models.MLModel.make_predictions
entries.notes: Batch inference. More efficient than repeated single predict calls.

entries.name: ct.utils.coreml_predict
entries.notes: One-shot load + predict utility. Convenient but slower for repeated calls (no model caching).

protocols.recipe:
import coremltools as ct
import numpy as np

def coreml_predict(model_path, input_dict):
    # Load CoreML model (uses ANE/GPU/CPU automatically)
    model = ct.models.MLModel(model_path, compute_units=ct.ComputeUnit.ALL)
    # Run inference
    result = model.predict(input_dict)
    return result

import coremltools as ct
import torch

def convert_pytorch_to_coreml(model, example_input, output_path):
    # model: torch.nn.Module in eval mode
    # example_input: torch.Tensor with correct shape
    model.eval()
    traced = torch.jit.trace(model, example_input)
    mlmodel = ct.convert(
        traced,
        inputs=[ct.TensorType(shape=example_input.shape)],
        convert_to='mlprogram',
        compute_units=ct.ComputeUnit.ALL,
    )
    mlmodel.save(output_path)
    return mlmodel
